title: Farm ERP acceptance design and implementation test backlog
purpose: Concrete acceptance contracts for the implementing agent. This file records no runtime test execution or passing result.

conventions.fixture_identity: Letters and fixture names are scenario labels, not fabricated production GUIDs. The implementation harness creates real records and records returned identifiers.
conventions.amounts: All numerical examples are synthetic. Decimal expected values are expressed in text exactly; implementations use the declared decimal arithmetic and amount precision, never binary floating point for postings.
conventions.tax_and_rates: Tax and foreign-exchange fixtures assert no current legal rate or market quote. Country activation needs its own reviewed evidence.
conventions.baseline_isolation: Each case runs in an isolated fixture or records a complete baseline so unrelated rows cannot change the expected controls.
conventions.owner_meaning: owner_component is the domain whose acceptance is being judged; collaborating_components retain their own table ownership and share the required outer transaction.
conventions.status_rule: Every case starts not_run. Evidence must record the actual source/build/runtime profile, actor/scope, operation inputs, before/after durable reads and outcome before status can change.
conventions.execution_rule: No runtime tests were performed when authoring this backlog. Playground checks alone do not prove production database concurrency, delivery, restore or regulated behavior.
conventions.release_rule: M00-M01 feed R0; R1 pilot ends M04; R2 native books ends M05; R3 enterprise workflows span M06-M10; R4 country/integration/offline/hardening/cutover/release spans M11-M15.
conventions.failure_rule: A failed command preserves its pre-command durable business state unless a case explicitly describes prior independent committed stages or an external uncertain outcome.
conventions.final_review_rule: Reference-document fixtures and static documentation checks are evidence for design quality, not substitutes for executing these cases on the implementation.
conventions.financial_mode_rule: M06-M10 ordinary domain cases can run after M04 in operational/export mode; their source quantities, values, claims and exports must reconcile. Expectations explicitly naming native journals/controls are repeated when native mode is enabled. Native-specific M05 cases are mandatory for R2 and full ERP release; absence of native accounting does not block otherwise independent operational enterprise development.

evidence_required_for_execution: JCB source/export revision and compiled extension checksums
Joomla/JCB/PHP/database versions, isolation and relevant configuration
Actor permissions, organisation/farm scope and fixture record IDs
Submitted command request key and redacted canonical payload
Before/after independent durable record reads and reconciled control totals
Screenshots or API result where the operator-visible outcome matters
Fault injection/concurrent connection schedule where applicable
Observed result, reviewer and any remaining limitation

cases.title: Approve an explicit discovery profile before implementation
preconditions: Farmer discovery identifies the actual legal entity, farms, enterprises, users, devices, current accounting system and hosting choice.
cases.action: Record and approve one discovery profile, including enabled initial country/currency, module scope, data sources and pilot acceptance actors.
expected_persistent_result: One versioned discovery profile identifies one legal entity and an explicit functional currency from NAD, ZAR or BWP.
Unknown facts are listed as unresolved decisions with an owner and activation consequence; no invented permit, wage, tax or bank-integration settings are approved.
No application business rows or external communications are created by this review.
failure_result: Any unresolved fact that determines a regulated capability prevents activation of that capability; implementation may continue on independently specified synthetic flows.

cases.title: Record the actual source and runtime compatibility profile
preconditions: The named JCB/Playground skills and three ERP documentation repositories are available for inspection.
cases.action: Persist the inspected repository SHAs and the intended Joomla, JCB, PHP, database engine/version, collation and isolation profile.
expected_persistent_result: One build profile distinguishes documentation revisions from runtime versions and observed capability from proposed behavior.
The implementation evidence register records no runtime case as passed merely because a reference repository contains a passing fixture.
Exact source identity and attribution are retained for any imported reusable artifact.
failure_result: A missing runtime version or unproven shared-class placement is an architecture blocker, not a successful compatibility claim.

cases.title: Compile native master/detail entities and database constraints
preconditions: A disposable Playground and a separate production-like test installation use the recorded build profile.
Native JCB definitions exist for a master and independently queryable detail view.
cases.action: Compile and install Core plus Ledger proof components; create one master with two detail records and inspect generated SQL and readback.
expected_persistent_result: Exactly one master and two distinct detail rows persist; each detail has its own numeric primary key and application GUID.
A detail GUID reference resolves to the correct master after export/import; JCB definition GUIDs remain separate from application record GUIDs.
Required unique keys, reference indexes and decimal/date types are present in the installed schema and are included in the build evidence.
failure_result: Missing constraints, JSON-only transactional children or generated-code hand edits fail the architecture gate.

cases.title: Rollback one cross-component command on the same connection
preconditions: Proof services for Core, Ledger and minimal Livestock participate in one outer unit of work.
One feed balance contains 10.000000 units worth NAD 100.00; no proof animal event or feed effects exist.
cases.action: Begin a Livestock proof command, insert an animal event, issue 2 feed units to its enterprise, enqueue an outbox intent, then inject an exception before final source state.
expected_persistent_result: After rollback, feed stock remains 10.000000 and value NAD 100.00.
No proof animal event, stock entry, valuation entry, journal, committed command result or outbox intent from the failed command remains.
Connection tracing records one participating database connection and no inner commit.
failure_result: Any surviving required effect or second connection used for synchronous owner writes fails the gate.

cases.title: Load shared contracts once and reject incompatible dependencies
preconditions: Core owns the shared contract namespace; Ledger and one satellite reference it.
The build profile defines a tested compatible contract version and an intentionally incompatible test version.
cases.action: Install components in documented order, resolve services in both callers, then attempt activation with the incompatible dependency profile.
expected_persistent_result: The compatible installation resolves the same owned contract without duplicate class definitions.
The incompatible combination does not activate dependent business commands and preserves existing records.
No separately hand-maintained runtime package is required outside the preserved JCB source.
failure_result: A duplicate class error, silent fallback to another implementation or partially enabled incompatible component fails the gate.

cases.title: Rebuild the proof installation solely from retained JCB source
preconditions: A verified proof build, its native JCB source/export and extension checksums are retained.
A fresh independent test environment has no generated output from the original build.
cases.action: Import the retained JCB source, compile, install and repeat the one-master/two-detail protected-command workflow.
expected_persistent_result: The same logical entities, relationships, permissions and protected behavior are present after rebuild.
One new master and exactly two linked detail rows persist in the fresh fixture.
Build receipts identify imported source, compiler/runtime profile, compiled checksum and operator evidence; no manual generated-file patch is needed.
failure_result: A missing Power, template, rule, relation or route that requires hand repair fails source portability.

cases.title: Use one party identity across customer and supplier roles
preconditions: Party P has one application GUID and no trade documents.
Authorized user may manage both customer and supplier roles.
cases.action: Add customer and supplier roles to P and create one sales draft and one purchase draft referencing P.
expected_persistent_result: Exactly one party row and two role relationships exist for P.
Both drafts reference the same party GUID while retaining their own document kind and child identities.
Changing P display name does not change its GUID or rewrite previously issued document address/name snapshots.
failure_result: Attempting to add the same overlapping role again is rejected or returns the existing relationship without a second active role.

cases.title: Enforce farm scope across lists, selectors, exports and API calls
preconditions: User U has stock-read permission for Farm A only.
One stock document belongs to Farm A and one to Farm B; both are in the same organisation.
cases.action: As U, query lists, modal selectors, report export and direct document routes using the known Farm B identifier.
expected_persistent_result: Only Farm A records are returned in every collection and export.
No Farm B document payload, filename, amount, internal note or linked target is disclosed.
No business record changes; denied attempts are recorded under the approved redaction policy.
failure_result: Any successful direct lookup or selector leak fails even if the normal navigation hides Farm B.

cases.title: Protect private evidence files and apply revocation immediately
preconditions: Private document D is linked to a Farm A record and its stored bytes have a known checksum.
User U initially has read access, then the user_scope grant is revoked.
cases.action: Download D while authorized, revoke access, then retry the same protected URL, guessed storage path, thumbnail and export attachment route.
expected_persistent_result: The authorized response checksum equals D original checksum.
Every post-revocation route refuses the private bytes and protected metadata without creating a public copy.
D, its link and evidentiary checksum remain unchanged; revocation is effective server-side without waiting for a page refresh.
failure_result: A reusable public storage URL, unprotected thumbnail or stale authorized session download fails the gate.

cases.title: Validate managed uploads without executing supplied content
preconditions: The approved file policy defines allowed types and maximum sizes for invoice and permit evidence.
Fixtures include a valid PDF, an oversized file, a MIME/extension mismatch and executable content disguised as an image.
cases.action: Submit each fixture through UI and direct upload endpoints, then inspect storage references and download behavior.
expected_persistent_result: Only the permitted PDF is accepted and linked to the authorized owning record with size, MIME and checksum.
Rejected fixtures create no active document link and no executable publicly served file.
A stored original cannot be overwritten silently by uploading another file with the same display name.
failure_result: Client-only validation, executable storage or cross-farm attachment linkage fails the gate.

cases.title: Replay a committed command and reject request-key payload changes
preconditions: Receipt command K for 5.000000 units has committed and its response was lost.
The unique receipt scope is organisation plus command type plus request key.
cases.action: Retry K unchanged, then retry K with quantity 6.000000.
expected_persistent_result: Unchanged K returns the stored receipt/result identity and creates zero additional stock, value, audit-business-effect or outbox-intent rows.
Changed K is rejected as a payload conflict; the original 5.000000-unit result and canonical payload hash remain unchanged.
failure_result: Returning a new receipt or replacing the prior result fails idempotency.

cases.title: Reject duplicate natural effects even with a different request key
preconditions: Sales invoice I revision 1 already has its unique source posting.
A second command uses a different request key but names the same source, line, effect kind and revision.
cases.action: Attempt the second source posting concurrently with an ordinary read of I.
expected_persistent_result: Exactly one effect set for I revision 1 persists.
No duplicate source values are accepted merely because the second command has a new transport key.
The independent read resolves I to the original durable result.
failure_result: A second balanced journal or duplicate stock movement fails the gate.

cases.title: Reject stale aggregate edits
preconditions: Two forms load draft D at version 5.
Writer A changes quantity to 7.000000 and commits version 6.
cases.action: Writer B submits its version-5 form with quantity 8.000000.
expected_persistent_result: D remains version 6 with quantity 7.000000.
Writer B receives a conflict identifying that a newer version exists without overwriting A changes.
No downstream posting is created from the rejected stale edit.
failure_result: A silent last-write-wins update or forced refresh that loses data fails the gate.

cases.title: Allocate unique document numbers under contention
preconditions: One document number series has next sequence 101.
Two independent commands issue distinct documents in the same organisation, kind and series.
cases.action: Run both issue operations concurrently, then cancel the first issued document and issue a third.
expected_persistent_result: The first two issued documents have distinct series numbers 101 and 102 in whichever commit order is accepted.
The third issued document receives 103; cancelling the first does not reuse 101.
Every issued/cancelled number resolves to one document; any permitted allocation gap has audit evidence.
failure_result: Duplicate numbers, silent sequence reset or number reuse fails the gate.

cases.title: Preserve packaging conversions and prohibit head-to-mass assumptions
preconditions: Feed product has a 25 kg bag conversion and base unit kg.
Cattle use head identity with independent kg weight observations.
cases.action: Receive 10 bags, then change the future bag specification to 20 kg; attempt to convert five cattle to stock kg through a generic fixed conversion.
expected_persistent_result: The issued receipt retains its factor 25 and base quantity 250.000000 kg.
A new draft may select the approved new factor 20 without changing the prior receipt.
No fixed head-to-kg conversion or additional cattle stock is created by a weight observation.
failure_result: Cross-dimensional conversion without an explicit valid measured product rule is rejected; historical receipt quantity remains unchanged.

cases.title: Blend weighted-average receipt value at the defined warehouse pool
preconditions: Pool P in Warehouse A contains 10.000000 units worth NAD 200.00.
A new receipt is 10.000000 units worth NAD 300.00 in a different lot of the same product.
cases.action: Post the receipt and then issue 4.000000 units from the physically eligible lot.
expected_persistent_result: P holds 20.000000 units and NAD 500.00 immediately after receipt, average NAD 25.000000.
The issue carries NAD 100.00; P then holds 16.000000 units and NAD 400.00.
Lot selection controls traceability, not an unconfigured different financial cost method.
failure_result: A failed receipt or issue leaves its complete pre-command quantity, value and source state unchanged.

cases.title: Serialize two issues against the last stock
preconditions: One eligible pool/lot has 10.000000 units and no reservations.
Two authorized different commands each request 6.000000 units.
cases.action: Synchronize both availability reads and execute the two issues under the implemented locking policy.
expected_persistent_result: Exactly one 6.000000-unit issue commits; on-hand becomes 4.000000.
The other command is rejected after rereading current availability or receives a bounded retry outcome that ultimately cannot post 6.000000.
There is one accepted source transition and one corresponding movement/value set.
failure_result: Negative quantity, two accepted issues, lost movement or stale absolute balance overwrite fails the gate.

cases.title: Create an absent stock balance safely under simultaneous receipts
preconditions: The exact product/lot/location/ownership balance key does not yet exist.
Receipt A is 3.000000 units at total NAD 30.00; receipt B is 4.000000 units at total NAD 80.00.
cases.action: Post both receipts concurrently against the previously absent balance.
expected_persistent_result: One balance row exists for the exact unique key, with 7.000000 units and aggregate value NAD 110.00.
Both distinct receipt movements persist exactly once.
The pool rate is derived from carried value and quantity at configured precision; rounded rate does not replace the exact NAD 110.00 value.
failure_result: Two balance rows, quantity 3 or 4, or only one receipt value fails the gate.

cases.title: Consume and release reservations exactly once
preconditions: Stock is 10.000000 units.
Order A reserves 7.000000; Order B has no reservation.
cases.action: Deliver 4.000000 for A, attempt to deliver 4.000000 for B, then cancel A remaining demand twice.
expected_persistent_result: After A delivery on-hand is 6.000000, A active reserved quantity is 3.000000 and freely available is 3.000000.
B request for 4.000000 is rejected.
After A cancellation, reservation is released once and available is 6.000000; the repeat cancellation creates no extra availability.
failure_result: Consuming another order reservation or releasing more than the outstanding claim fails the gate.

cases.title: Conserve owned stock through dispatch and transit receipt
preconditions: Warehouse A contains 10.000000 units worth NAD 250.00; owned transit and Warehouse B are empty.
cases.action: Dispatch 2.000000 to transit, stop before receipt, then receive the same transfer at B and retry receipt.
expected_persistent_result: After dispatch A has 8.000000/NAD 200.00 and transit has 2.000000/NAD 50.00; B remains zero.
After receipt A remains 8.000000/NAD 200.00, transit is zero and B has 2.000000/NAD 50.00.
Organisation total stays 10.000000/NAD 250.00; duplicate receipt creates no extra pair.
failure_result: Injected failure inside either stage leaves that whole stage uncommitted; a dispatch header cannot disagree with its paired source/transit effects.

cases.title: Distinguish physical lot holds from valuation and FEFO picking
preconditions: Product P has two lots in one valuation pool: L1 quantity 4.000000 expires 2027-04-10; L2 quantity 6.000000 expires 2027-04-20.
L1 is quarantined; both lots are included in physical on-hand.
cases.action: On 2027-04-09 request a normal sale issue of 5.000000 using FEFO, then attempt direct issue from L1.
expected_persistent_result: Normal picking selects 5.000000 from L2; total remaining on-hand is 5.000000, including quarantined L1 quantity 4.000000.
L1 remains unchanged and ineligible for ordinary sale; direct issue is denied under the same policy.
Financial cost uses the shared pool method and is not changed to lot-specific FIFO by the selector.
failure_result: Counting all physical stock as freely available or bypassing hold through a direct route fails the gate.

cases.title: Reconcile a stale physical count with intervening movements
preconditions: Count session records 10.000000 at cutoff T1.
A legitimate later issue of 2.000000 commits at T2; current balance is 8.000000.
The counter observation of 9.000000 is explicitly stated to be at T1.
cases.action: Attempt to post the old count unchanged after T2, then approve a reconciled count correction using its cutoff and intervening issue.
expected_persistent_result: The unreconciled stale submission is rejected for review.
The approved discrepancy is minus 1.000000 at the permitted posting boundary, leaving current on-hand 7.000000 after the legitimate 2.000000 issue.
The count retains observation time, original snapshot, intervening movement reference, approval and correction identity.
failure_result: Setting the current balance directly to 9.000000 or deleting the intervening issue fails the gate.

cases.title: Match partial receipts and supplier bills by source line
preconditions: Purchase order has one line for 10.000000 units at NAD 100.00 each; over-receipt and over-bill tolerances are zero.
Six units have been received; no bill has been approved.
cases.action: Approve a bill for six units, then attempt another bill for five against the same received source line.
expected_persistent_result: The first bill is NAD 600.00 with quantity 6.000000 linked to the actual receipt and order line.
Four ordered units remain unreceived; zero received units remain unbilled.
The second five-unit bill is rejected without changing stock, payable or billed quantity.
failure_result: Matching only by product, billing the same received quantity twice or silently exceeding tolerance fails the gate.

cases.title: Close a farmers market shift with a separate shortage
preconditions: Opening cash is NAD 200.00.
Posted sales include NAD 500.00 cash and NAD 300.00 electronic tender; a linked NAD 50.00 cash refund exists.
Cashier counts NAD 640.00.
cases.action: Close the shift and request approval of the cash difference.
expected_persistent_result: Expected drawer cash is NAD 650.00; counted cash is NAD 640.00; shortage is NAD 10.00.
Electronic tender NAD 300.00 is tracked separately from cash and from bank settlement.
One reasoned shortage adjustment is created only on approval; original sales, refunds and opening float stay immutable.
failure_result: Editing the opening float to hide the shortage, or treating electronic tender as drawer cash, is rejected.

cases.title: Export a complete operational pilot without claiming native books
preconditions: Organisation is in operational/export mode.
Approved trade, payment and stock records exist with stable GUIDs and currency snapshots.
A customer display name starts with an equals sign.
cases.action: Generate the accountant export twice at the same source watermark and inspect the UI/report menu and exported text fields.
expected_persistent_result: Each artifact identifies schema version, source watermark, record GUIDs, functional/document currencies and exact control totals.
The two exports represent the same source population; generating them creates no journal or duplicate payable.
Spreadsheet-dangerous text is safely serialized without changing the underlying business name.
No statutory trial balance or native-posted claim is exposed in operational mode.
failure_result: Missing source rows, duplicate effects, spreadsheet formula execution or false native-book status fails the pilot gate.

cases.title: Complete the minimum pilot livestock and task slice
preconditions: Pilot has one farm, two individually identified cattle, an authorized supervisor and a worker task view.
Full later breeding and payroll capabilities are disabled.
cases.action: Create one cattle-check task, record one weight observation for each animal, complete the task and review the daily workspace.
expected_persistent_result: Exactly two animals remain; two new weight observations and one completed task persist.
No extra head count, medicine issue, payroll payment or animal valuation journal is created by weight/task capture.
The worker sees only assigned operational details and the owner can trace completion to the actor and time.
failure_result: Needing JCB configuration screens for routine capture or silently generating financial effects fails the pilot workflow.

cases.title: Post purchase receipt, bill and payment with reconciled controls
preconditions: Native accounting is active with mapped inventory, receipt-clearing, payable and bank accounts in an open period.
Taxes are disabled in this synthetic fixture.
cases.action: Receive goods worth NAD 1,000.00, approve the matching supplier bill and pay NAD 1,000.00.
expected_persistent_result: Receipt posts inventory debit 1,000.00 and receipt-clearing credit 1,000.00.
Bill posts receipt-clearing debit 1,000.00 and payable credit 1,000.00.
Payment posts payable debit 1,000.00 and bank credit 1,000.00.
Final inventory is 1,000.00, receipt clearing and supplier residual are zero, and every event has one balanced journal/source link.
failure_result: Any stage missing an account mapping is refused without a partial source or journal transition; previous independently committed stages remain intact.

cases.title: Post delivery, invoice and receipt as distinct events
preconditions: Goods carrying NAD 600.00 are available; sale price is NAD 1,000.00; taxes disabled.
Native mappings and period are valid.
cases.action: Deliver the goods, issue the invoice and allocate a NAD 1,000.00 receipt.
expected_persistent_result: Delivery debits cost of sales 600.00 and credits inventory 600.00.
Invoice debits receivables 1,000.00 and credits revenue 1,000.00.
Receipt debits bank/cash 1,000.00 and credits receivables 1,000.00; invoice remainder is zero.
Gross margin is NAD 400.00; cash receipt, revenue and inventory relief remain separately attributable.
failure_result: Invoicing cannot automatically create a second delivery or repeating receipt cannot create extra cash.

cases.title: Rollback stock and finance after a late posting failure
preconditions: Direct market sale command combines a 2.000000-unit stock issue, invoice, cash receipt and journals.
Pre-command stock is 5.000000 units worth NAD 250.00; cash and sale effects for this command are zero.
cases.action: Inject an exception after creating stock/value effects but before the final journal and source commit.
expected_persistent_result: Independent read after rollback shows stock 5.000000 and value NAD 250.00.
No invoice, receipt, cash entry, journal, final source state, command result or outbox intent from the failed sale remains.
Retry with the same request key after the failure can produce one complete valid sale.
failure_result: An orphaned posted invoice, stock deduction or partial journal is a release blocker.

cases.title: Serialize period closing against an in-flight posting
preconditions: Period P is open and contains no effects from command K.
A posting command K and a close command C target P concurrently.
cases.action: Pause K after loading P, execute C, then resume under the implemented shared period-lock protocol; repeat with the opposite lock order.
expected_persistent_result: If K owns the lock first, its complete posting commits before C finalizes and C reconciles a population including K.
If C closes first, K is rejected or restarted and then rejected; K adds zero effects dated in closed P.
No accepted outcome contains a journal committed into P after its lock without an authorized reopening record.
failure_result: An unlocked read of open state followed by a post-close write fails the gate.

cases.title: Serialize payment allocation against the invoice remainder
preconditions: Invoice I has NAD 100.00 outstanding.
Two available payments each contain NAD 100.00 and are not yet allocated.
cases.action: Submit full allocations of both payments to I concurrently.
expected_persistent_result: Exactly NAD 100.00 is allocated to I; its remainder becomes zero.
Only one payment is fully consumed; the other existing payment retains NAD 100.00 unallocated.
No duplicate allocation or negative invoice remainder persists.
failure_result: Both requests reading the old remainder and allocating NAD 200.00 fails the gate.

cases.title: Preserve invoice-level residuals when applying a credit
preconditions: Invoice I is NAD 300.00; payment allocation is NAD 200.00; tax disabled.
A mapped return draft originally copied three units but is edited to one unit at NAD 100.00.
cases.action: Recompute and issue the NAD 100.00 credit, first as unapplied credit, then explicitly allocate it to I.
expected_persistent_result: Before allocation I has NAD 100.00 due and the credit has NAD 100.00 available, even though net party balance is zero.
After allocation both document residuals are zero; original invoice, payment and credit identities remain distinct.
Credit validation uses its recomputed NAD 100.00 total, not the stale mapped NAD 300.00 total.
failure_result: A zero net customer balance alone cannot mark I settled; editing the posted invoice or credit is refused.

cases.title: Recognize foreign receivable settlement gain
preconditions: Functional currency NAD; sales invoice BWP 1,000.00 at approved rate 1 BWP = NAD 1.350000000000.
Settlement is from a NAD bank at 1 BWP = NAD 1.400000000000; no tax or bank fee.
cases.action: Issue the invoice and settle it fully using the second rate.
expected_persistent_result: Invoice stores BWP 1,000.00, NAD 1,350.00 and its original rate snapshot.
Settlement debits bank NAD 1,400.00, credits receivable NAD 1,350.00 and credits realized exchange gain NAD 50.00.
Both invoice currency and base residuals are zero; later rate edits do not rewrite either event.
failure_result: Substituting the payment rate into the invoice or recognizing NAD 1,400.00 sales revenue fails the gate.

cases.title: Recognize foreign payable settlement loss separately from fees
preconditions: Functional currency NAD; supplier bill BWP 1,000.00 carried at NAD 1,350.00.
Settlement requires NAD 1,400.00 plus an explicitly recorded NAD 10.00 bank fee.
cases.action: Post the supplier settlement and bank fee.
expected_persistent_result: Debit payable NAD 1,350.00, debit exchange loss NAD 50.00, debit bank-fee expense NAD 10.00 and credit bank NAD 1,410.00.
The supplier foreign/base residuals are zero and the bank statement reconciles to NAD 1,410.00.
Invoice rate, settlement rate and fee source remain separately inspectable.
failure_result: Hiding the fee inside the exchange difference or leaving an unexplained base residual fails the gate.

cases.title: Clear a final partial-payment rounding residual deterministically
preconditions: Foreign invoice face amount is BWP 3.00 with exact approved rate 1 BWP = NAD 1.333333333333; carried base total is NAD 4.00.
Two BWP 1.00 payments have each released NAD 1.33 under the declared allocation policy; remaining base carrying amount is NAD 1.34.
cases.action: Settle the final BWP 1.00 using the same approved rate and a NAD 1.33 bank settlement.
expected_persistent_result: Final allocation releases the whole NAD 1.34 carrying remainder and BWP 1.00 foreign remainder.
Final settlement debits bank NAD 1.33 and the approved settlement-rounding/exchange-loss account NAD 0.01, and credits receivable NAD 1.34.
Both residuals become exactly zero; total released carrying value is NAD 4.00, not NAD 3.99.
failure_result: Leaving a phantom one-cent receivable or silently altering prior settlements fails the gate.

cases.title: Reject missing, future-only and ambiguous rate/tax versions
preconditions: A foreign draft dated 2027-01-10 has no approved rate applicable on that date; a later rate begins 2027-01-11.
A second fixture deliberately has two overlapping approved tax versions for the same use.
cases.action: Attempt to issue each draft, then resolve each reference-data problem through an authorized dated approval and retry.
expected_persistent_result: Initial requests create no posted document, stock effect, journal or final command result.
No future-only rate or implicit rate 1 is selected; ambiguous tax selection is refused.
After correction, exactly one issued document per command uses one recorded applicable rate/tax version.
failure_result: Fallback to a convenient later rate, arbitrary overlapping rule or mixed tax snapshots fails the gate.

cases.title: Keep historic stock order fixed while recording a late real-world event
preconditions: A pool has a posted receipt followed by a costed delivery in period P.
Initial release policy forbids historical cost reorder/replay; current open period is Q.
cases.action: Attempt to insert an earlier cost-affecting stock entry before the delivery, then submit an approved current-period correction with the true occurrence date retained.
expected_persistent_result: Backdated reorder is refused and every original valuation/journal row stays unchanged.
The authorized correction is a new linked effect in Q with original occurrence date, reason and approver.
Reports distinguish real occurrence, posting date and adjustment; no unimplemented background cost replay is scheduled.
failure_result: Accepting the historical date while leaving dependent later costs stale fails the gate.

cases.title: Deplete a weighted-average pool without manufacturing value
preconditions: An initially empty pool receives 54.000000 jars at aggregate NAD 900.00 and has no other receipts.
Amount rounding is half-up to two decimals with a deterministic final-depletion rule.
cases.action: Issue 20.000000 jars, then issue the final 34.000000.
expected_persistent_result: First issue value is NAD 333.33, leaving 34.000000 jars worth NAD 566.67.
Final issue value is NAD 566.67, leaving quantity 0.000000 and value NAD 0.00.
Total issued value equals NAD 900.00 even though the displayed unit rate is rounded to six places.
failure_result: Multiplying a rounded NAD 16.67 by 54 to invent NAD 900.18, or leaving nonzero value at zero stock, fails the gate.

cases.title: Revalue only eligible open monetary items at period end
preconditions: Open receivable BWP 1,000.00 carries NAD 1,350.00.
Approved closing rate is 1 BWP = NAD 1.380000000000.
A purchased inventory pool carries NAD 1,350.00 and is not eligible for currency revaluation.
cases.action: Run approved monetary revaluation and rerun the same period revision.
expected_persistent_result: One adjustment raises the receivable carrying amount to NAD 1,380.00 with NAD 30.00 unrealized gain under the approved template.
Inventory remains NAD 1,350.00 with unchanged quantity and historical acquisition basis.
Rerun adds zero duplicate adjustment; unwind/reversal retains a link to that period revision.
failure_result: Revaluing nonmonetary stock or duplicating the period adjustment fails the gate.

cases.title: Post each asset depreciation period once
preconditions: Asset cost NAD 12,000.00, residual NAD 2,000.00, approved five full annual straight-line periods, no prior depreciation or prorating.
cases.action: Post the five scheduled annual charges and repeat the command for the third period.
expected_persistent_result: Each period posts NAD 2,000.00 expense/depreciation control; total accumulated depreciation is NAD 10,000.00.
Ending carrying amount is NAD 2,000.00; historical schedule rows retain their journal links.
Repeating period three produces no new journal or schedule charge.
failure_result: Changing a future useful-life estimate cannot overwrite already posted periods; a missing mapping prevents that period posting.

cases.title: Apply a synthetic effective-dated tax rule and exact rounding
preconditions: Synthetic rule T1 is 10 percent through 2027-06-30; T2 is 12 percent from 2027-07-01, with half-open validity and approved status.
Each fixture invoice has one NAD 100.00 tax-exclusive line and no discount.
cases.action: Issue one invoice on 2027-06-30 and one on 2027-07-01, then revise a future tax master and attempt generic edit of the issued invoices.
expected_persistent_result: First invoice retains net NAD 100.00, tax NAD 10.00, gross NAD 110.00 and T1 identity.
Second retains net NAD 100.00, tax NAD 12.00, gross NAD 112.00 and T2 identity.
Issued tax detail and totals remain unchanged by later master edits or generic CRUD.
failure_result: Wrong boundary version, binary-float imbalance or post-issue mutation fails; these synthetic rates are never activated as country law.

cases.title: Conserve grouped livestock through births, losses and split
preconditions: Unindividualized sheep group G has 20 head.
No individual animal rows represent those 20 head.
cases.action: Record 3 births, 2 deaths, sale/dispatch of 4 head and split 5 remaining head into new group H.
expected_persistent_result: G progresses 20 -> 23 -> 21 -> 17 -> 12; H ends with 5.
Combined live owned group count is 17; event history explains births +3, deaths -2 and sold -4 without counting the internal split as loss.
Every confirmed event has one source identity and repeat submission adds zero head changes.
failure_result: Negative count, silent group replacement or double-counting both split source and destination fails the gate.

cases.title: Individualize animals without counting them twice
preconditions: Unindividualized group G has 10 head.
No existing animal identities match the four animals to be registered.
cases.action: Convert four group head into four individually identified animals and assign them to a management group.
expected_persistent_result: Unindividualized count becomes 6 and exactly four animal rows are created; total owned head stays 10.
Management-group membership contributes a grouping view, not four additional stock-count events.
Repeated conversion of the same source allocation does not create more animals.
failure_result: Persisting 10 unindividualized head plus four new independent head fails the gate.

cases.title: Preserve animal identity through tag changes and birth replay
preconditions: Animal A has active identifier 000123 under a scheme that enforces uniqueness.
Dam D and sire S are registered; neither has a parent cycle.
cases.action: Replace A tag with 000456, attempt duplicate active use of 000456, then record the same calf birth twice with one source key and attempt cyclic parentage.
expected_persistent_result: A retains one GUID and two dated identifier-history rows, preserving leading zeroes; old tag remains historical.
Exactly one calf animal and one birth event persist for the repeated birth source.
The duplicate active tag and parent cycle are rejected without partial identifier or parent updates.
failure_result: Using mutable tag text as the primary animal identity or creating a second calf on retry fails the gate.

cases.title: Enforce purpose-specific withdrawal at the exact boundary
preconditions: Animal A has an approved synthetic sale-for-slaughter hold ending 2027-01-17T08:00:00Z, equivalent to 10:00 local in the fixture zone.
Movement authority and all other eligibility rules are satisfied.
cases.action: Attempt slaughter dispatch at one second before the hold end and at the exact hold end using UI and direct command routes.
expected_persistent_result: Early dispatch is refused with zero stock/custody movement; the animal and hold records remain unchanged.
At the exact end, one authorized dispatch may commit and its eligibility snapshot names the rule and release instant.
The fixture rule is not represented as an actual medicine recommendation or blanket permission for unrelated purposes.
failure_result: Timezone ambiguity, UI-only validation or treating an absent withdrawal rule as zero days fails the gate.

cases.title: Finalize treatment and medicine consumption atomically
preconditions: A draft treatment targets a snapshot of animals A and B.
Medicine lot M has 10.000000 eligible units; actual recorded use is 2.000000.
All clinically supplied instruction/withdrawal metadata is present and approved for the fixture.
cases.action: Finalize treatment, inject a medicine-post failure in one run, then post successfully and later move B to another herd.
expected_persistent_result: Failed run leaves treatment draft and medicine at 10.000000 with no finalized withdrawal targets.
Successful run leaves medicine 8.000000, one finalized treatment and exactly targets A and B.
Later herd changes do not alter who received the treatment or duplicate stock consumption.
failure_result: Treatment finalization without its required stock effect, missing target snapshot or automatic clinical inference fails the gate.

cases.title: Separate animal ownership, custody, movement authority and invoice
preconditions: Animal A is farm-owned at Farm A with purchase cost recorded.
A sale invoice draft exists, but required movement evidence for destination B is unapproved.
cases.action: Try dispatch, approve valid evidence for the exact subject/date/destination, dispatch to transit and receive at B; separately test an internal owned farm transfer.
expected_persistent_result: Initial dispatch is refused; invoice draft alone changes no physical location or custody.
Approved dispatch/receipt each persist one linked movement stage and evidence snapshot.
Internal transfer preserves total owned head and creates no sale revenue; custody changes do not silently change ownership.
failure_result: Uploading an unreviewed file or paying an invoice cannot bypass movement eligibility.

cases.title: Distinguish mortality from sale and preserve confirmed events
preconditions: Animal A is alive and owned; its current group membership is active.
No mortality or disposal has been recorded.
cases.action: Confirm mortality with date/reason/evidence, retry, then attempt a normal sale dispatch and generic deletion of the mortality event.
expected_persistent_result: One mortality event persists, A is not live available stock and live head count falls by one exactly once.
No revenue or customer invoice is automatically created.
Sale dispatch and generic deletion are refused; any correction uses an authorized linked amendment.
failure_result: A second mortality decrement or restoration by editing a published flag fails the gate.

cases.title: Create crop schedules without inventing stock or cost
preconditions: Crop template has two tasks at days 2-4 and 9-12; cycle starts 2027-04-01.
No actual inputs, labour or harvest are recorded.
cases.action: Create the cycle and tasks, save it twice, then revise the reusable template.
expected_persistent_result: One cycle and exactly two cycle task instances exist, dated 2027-04-02 to 2027-04-04 and 2027-04-09 to 2027-04-12.
No stock movements, harvest receipts, labour actuals or financial costs are created by the plan.
Existing task snapshots remain attributable to the template revision used; future template changes do not rewrite completed work.
failure_result: Duplicate task creation on save or expected yield posted as real stock fails the gate.

cases.title: Block harvest under an approved input restriction
preconditions: Plot P has a draft input application carrying an approved synthetic rule that will restrict harvest until 2027-05-20T08:00:00Z when finalized.
The recorded input lot has sufficient stock, actual use is 1.500000 units, and this draft has not yet consumed stock. A separate independent draft is used for injected failure.
cases.action: Post input use, attempt harvest one second before release and at the boundary; inject stock failure during a separate input-finalization run.
expected_persistent_result: Successful input finalization consumes exactly 1.500000 and records one plot/cycle application and restriction snapshot.
Early harvest creates no finished lot or stock receipt; boundary harvest can commit if all other checks pass.
Failed input stock posting leaves no finalized application or half-created hold.
failure_result: Direct API harvest bypass, duplicated application consumption or missing restriction treated as zero duration fails the gate.

cases.title: Post harvest grades and waste with one approved cost allocation
preconditions: Cycle C has an approved attributable cost pool NAD 1,100.00.
Harvest actual is 100.000000 kg: 80.000000 saleable and 20.000000 recorded process/grade loss.
Fixture policy assigns the full 1,100.00 to saleable output and posts loss quantity without fictitious value.
cases.action: Finalize harvest, transfer 10.000000 kg for internal lodge use and sell 15.000000 kg at NAD 30.00/kg.
expected_persistent_result: Finalized harvest receives 80.000000 saleable kg worth NAD 1,100.00 and records 20.000000 loss separately; no second 100 kg receipt is also counted.
The approved per-saleable-kg cost basis is NAD 13.750000; internal transfer creates no external revenue.
After the transfer and sale, market stock is 55.000000 kg; sales net value is NAD 450.00.
failure_result: Posting both gross and net harvest, creating stock for waste or duplicating the crop cost as a new expense fails the gate.

cases.title: Retain observation identity, units and missing-value meaning
preconditions: A field sample has collection, test and result instants and a canonical numeric value with unit.
A second field-day has no rainfall observation; a third has an explicit 0.000000 mm reading.
cases.action: Import the same sample twice, display it under decimal-dot and decimal-comma locales, and query the rain report.
expected_persistent_result: One sample observation persists and its numeric value/unit does not change with display locale.
Collection <= test <= result is enforced; invalid temporal order creates no approved result.
The report distinguishes missing rainfall from a measured zero; neither observation creates an input purchase or treatment recommendation.
failure_result: Duplicate sample links changing aggregates, locale-dependent numeric decisions or invented zero readings fails the gate.

cases.title: Freeze recipe revisions and reject recursive BOMs
preconditions: Approved recipe R1 produces 10 units from defined material/packaging quantities.
Production order P is released against R1.
cases.action: Create R2 with changed quantities, attempt to edit R1 in place, and attempt a multilevel cycle A -> B -> A in a capability-enabled fixture.
expected_persistent_result: P retains R1 identity and original planned quantities; R2 is a separate revision for future orders.
In-place mutation of a used approved revision is rejected.
Recursive recipe activation/explosion is rejected without partial demand or work-order creation.
failure_result: A recipe edit rewriting historical actuals or unbounded recursive explosion fails the gate.

cases.title: Post workshop production and sale with cost conserved
preconditions: Actual timber cost is NAD 500.00, bought parts NAD 100.00 and approved conversion cost NAD 200.00.
There are no valued by-products, prior finished stock or other receipts; actual output is 10 units.
The ordinary domain acceptance profile is operational/export mode after M04; repeat financial effects under native accounting when that capability is enabled.
cases.action: Finalize the batch, release quality, deliver and invoice six units at NAD 150.00 each.
expected_persistent_result: One production event consumes the selected input lots and receives 10 units at total NAD 800.00.
Sale value is NAD 900.00, output cost relieved is NAD 480.00, gross margin is NAD 420.00 and remaining finished stock is four units worth NAD 320.00.

Conversion cost is attributed once. In operational mode the exact cost source appears once in approved export; in native mode absorption offsets the approved expense/clearing basis once instead of charging a second labour expense.
failure_result: Any missing input, mapping or required quality result rolls back the complete required production command.

cases.title: Separate actual zero input cost from a missing cost basis
preconditions: Fixture A consumes a legitimately approved zero-value input and NAD 90.00 eligible conversion cost for 90 output units.
Fixture B has an unknown input-cost basis with no approved fallback; the finished product historical display rate is NAD 12.00.
cases.action: Complete production under A and attempt completion under B.
expected_persistent_result: A receives 90 units at aggregate NAD 90.00, unit basis NAD 1.000000; zero is retained as a real input cost.
B remains incomplete with no stock/valuation/journal effects until its missing basis is resolved.
Neither path silently substitutes the historical NAD 12.00 rate solely because input arithmetic is zero or missing.
failure_result: Conflating null and zero or silently inventing a finished inventory value fails the gate.

cases.title: Allocate main, secondary and recovered output value once
preconditions: Consumed material cost NAD 1,000.00; separately valued recovered output NAD 100.00.
Remaining material cost shares are primary 80 percent and secondary 20 percent; eligible conversion cost NAD 90.00 is assigned only to primary.
Primary output quantity is 90 units.
cases.action: Finalize the batch and rerun the same completion command.
expected_persistent_result: Recovered output receives NAD 100.00; secondary output receives NAD 180.00; primary output receives NAD 810.00, or NAD 9.000000 per primary unit.
Total output value is NAD 1,090.00, equal to material plus conversion; no double deduction of recovered output occurs.
Retry changes no quantities, values or allocation rows.
failure_result: Cost shares outside their required total, recovered value above allowed pool or unexplained negative primary cost blocks completion.

cases.title: Preserve partial production cost and prohibit double consumption
preconditions: Order plans 10 outputs; approved material pool is NAD 500.00.
All materials have moved to work in progress, but only the portion attributable to four outputs is consumed/assigned in the first partial run under the declared fixture method.
cases.action: Receive four outputs at total NAD 200.00, then complete six outputs at total NAD 300.00; retry each partial command.
expected_persistent_result: After first run four outputs carry NAD 200.00 and remaining attributable work in progress is NAD 300.00.
After completion all 10 outputs carry aggregate NAD 500.00 and work-in-progress remainder is zero.
Each partial run has distinct actual/source identities; retries duplicate neither consumption nor receipt.
failure_result: Job-card completion independently creating another receipt, or reusing all original consumption cost on both partial runs, fails the gate.

cases.title: Trace recall through production, rework and deliveries
preconditions: Input lot A feeds output lot B; some B feeds reworked lot C.
B and C have both remaining stock and delivered sales lines; a separate lot D has no path from A.
Recorded genealogy proves batch membership only, not individual-jar allocations.
cases.action: Open a recall for A and query upstream/downstream lots, remaining balances and distribution destinations.
expected_persistent_result: A, B and C are included in affected scope; D is excluded.
All remaining affected saleable quantities are held and known B/C delivery recipients are identified by source lines.
The report states batch-level possible exposure and makes no unsupported claim that a particular jar excluded A.
Attempt to introduce a genealogy cycle is rejected.
failure_result: Missing rework descendants, double-counted stock through joins or unapproved release of held outputs fails the gate.

cases.title: Reject lot-state changes through generic CRUD and API bypass
preconditions: Output lot L is in quality hold and lacks one required approved quality result.
User has ordinary production write rights but lacks quality-release authority.
cases.action: Try normal release, direct status update, bulk publish, save-as-copy and direct sale issue of L.
expected_persistent_result: Every bypass refuses release/issue and leaves quality state, stock, value and genealogy unchanged.
Only the designated release command by an authorized role with all required evidence can change L eligibility.
The audit identifies denied action and actor without exposing protected lab details unnecessarily.
failure_result: A Joomla published flag, generated model save or API allowlist omission that releases L fails the gate.

cases.title: Price and occupy lodging with half-open room nights
preconditions: Two physical rooms are available for local nights 2027-06-10 and 2027-06-11.
Per-room nightly rates are NAD 900.00 and NAD 1,100.00 respectively; taxes disabled.
cases.action: Confirm a two-room stay arriving 2027-06-10 and departing 2027-06-12, then quote a new arrival on 2027-06-12.
expected_persistent_result: First stay stores four room-night claims and net price NAD 4,000.00.
No night of 2027-06-12 is consumed by the first stay.
New arrival can claim the departure-date night if operational turnaround/block rules permit it; price and occupancy use the same interval convention.
failure_result: Departure-inclusive occupancy or counting three charged nights fails the gate.

cases.title: Share capacity across package aliases and concurrent bookings
preconditions: Only room R is sellable on night N.
Packages P1 and P2 both reference R; two clerks independently request the night through different packages.
cases.action: Confirm both requests concurrently.
expected_persistent_result: Exactly one active room-night claim for R/N exists; exactly one confirmation succeeds.
The losing booking retains an explainable unconfirmed/conflict state with zero committed replacement claim.
Capacity is never duplicated merely because two saleable products/packages name the same physical room.
failure_result: Two confirmations, negative available capacity or an orphaned synchronous deposit allocation fails the gate.

cases.title: Resolve expiry and confirmation of a hold atomically
preconditions: Hold H expires at 2027-06-01T10:00:00Z and owns one room-night claim.
A confirmation and expiry worker compete at that exact boundary.
cases.action: Run both operations with the server clock fixed to the expiry instant and repeat with confirmation committed just before expiry.
expected_persistent_result: At the expiry instant H is no longer eligible to confirm without reacquiring capacity; expiry releases its hold once.
If confirmation committed before expiry, the later expiry worker does not release the confirmed claim.
No outcome has confirmed booking status without its active claim, or a released claim still counted as held.
failure_result: Client clock authority, unconditional expiry release or a confirmed expired hold fails the gate.

cases.title: Move a confirmed stay without losing the existing reservation
preconditions: Booking B owns room R on nights 10 and 11 June.
Requested replacement room S has the first replacement night free and the second blocked.
cases.action: Attempt to move the whole stay to S, then remove the block and retry with a new authorized command.
expected_persistent_result: Failed move leaves both original R claims and accepted price/policy snapshots unchanged, with zero partial S claims.
Successful move atomically creates both S claims, releases both R claims and increments B version once.
Repeated successful request key returns the same move result.
failure_result: Releasing old claims before securing the complete replacement or partially moving the stay fails the gate.

cases.title: Keep deposits, cancellation fees and refunds separately attributable
preconditions: Booking B has a received NAD 1,000.00 deposit in operational/export mode; the same commercial fixture is repeated in native mode when enabled.
Accepted synthetic cancellation policy requires a NAD 200.00 fee; no accommodation service has been earned.
cases.action: Cancel B, approve the fee and refund the remaining NAD 800.00; retry cancellation and refund.
expected_persistent_result: Booking resource claims are released once.

The NAD 1,000.00 deposit source balance is fully disposed through the documented NAD 200.00 fee/application and NAD 800.00 refund path. In native mode the same actions clear the deposit liability; operational mode makes no posted-GL claim.
Net bank change from original receipt and refund is plus NAD 200.00; cancellation does not delete the original receipt or recognize accommodation revenue.
Retries create no duplicate fee, claim release or refund.
failure_result: Marking a refund complete without payment evidence or deleting an externally settled deposit fails the gate.

cases.title: Coordinate guides and vehicles with explicit time buffers
preconditions: Guide G and vehicle V are claimed from 06:00 to 12:00 local time.
Resource policy requires a 30-minute turnaround after this booking.
Work can expose V maintenance availability through an optional capability, but Stay owns reservation claims.
cases.action: Request 09:00-13:00, then 12:00-14:00, then 12:30-14:00 for both resources.
expected_persistent_result: The overlapping and buffer-violating requests create zero claims.
The 12:30 request may acquire both resources atomically if no other block exists.
Disabling the optional Work capability does not duplicate physical resources or erase existing claims; required unavailable eligibility is surfaced.
failure_result: Claiming only one resource on failure, ignoring a blocking maintenance interval or creating separate capacity per package fails the gate.

cases.title: Prevent hunting quota over-allocation and expired approval use
preconditions: Approved species/farm/season quota ceiling is 2 with one unit already reserved and none consumed.
Two hunt requests each seek one remaining unit; approval validity ends at the stated season boundary.
cases.action: Allocate both concurrently, then attempt confirmation with approval expired.
expected_persistent_result: Only one new unit is reserved; total reserved plus consumed is at most 2.
The losing request has no quota allocation and cannot infer availability from a wildlife observation.
Expired approval blocks confirmation even if numerical quota remains; review evidence is tied to the applicable subject and dates.
failure_result: Quota double-spend, use of expired approval or treating an uploaded file as automatic approval fails the gate.

cases.title: Separate hunt booking, actual outcome and trophy custody
preconditions: A lodging stay and guide-service invoice are paid; hunt outcome has not occurred.
Required hunt-specific permissions/evidence are not yet approved.
cases.action: Attempt to record a completed hunt from invoice status alone, then perform the authorized workflow after valid approval and record an actual outcome/custody handoff.
expected_persistent_result: Payment creates no automatic wildlife decrement, harvest outcome or trophy record.
The authorized actual outcome consumes the relevant quota allocation once and retains person/species/date/location evidence.
Trophy custody handoff records source, recipient, date and external permit references without claiming ERP-issued government authorization.
failure_result: Cancelling the booking cannot erase a previously confirmed real outcome or restore consumed quota without an authorized correction.

cases.title: Keep personnel and banking data out of ordinary task access
preconditions: Supervisor U may assign tasks and view workers but has no salary, private personnel or bank-detail permission.
Worker W has restricted HR attachments, bank information and approved pay data.
cases.action: As U open task lists, worker selectors, search, CSV export, direct worker/detail routes and attachment URLs.
expected_persistent_result: Operational worker identity and task availability are visible only as permitted.
Salary, bank account, private identifiers and HR document bytes are absent or denied across all paths.
No private field can be changed by submitting it in an ordinary task update payload.
failure_result: Field-level leak through an API/export or mass-assignment write fails the gate.

cases.title: Separate reviewed labour cost from payroll entitlement
preconditions: Worker W records 6.000000 cattle hours and 2.000000 workshop hours at approved costing rate NAD 50.000000/hour.
These time spans do not overlap; the next-day rate changes to NAD 60.000000.
cases.action: Approve both entries, change the future rate and attempt an incompatible overlapping attendance/time record.
expected_persistent_result: Approved internal costs remain cattle NAD 300.00 and workshop NAD 100.00, total NAD 400.00.
Historical rate snapshots stay NAD 50.000000; future rate affects only applicable future entries.
An incompatible overlap is rejected or requires an explicit authorized correction; no automatic payroll payable is created from management cost alone.
failure_result: Repricing approved history or counting one attendance span twice as payable work fails the gate.

cases.title: Export one reviewed payroll period and deduplicate approved import
preconditions: Period P has approved attendance, leave and adjustment inputs with no unresolved approvals.
Native statutory payroll calculation is disabled; an external approved payroll response specifies payable NAD 1,875.00 and employer liability NAD 10.01.
cases.action: Export P twice at the same revision, import the approved external result twice, then attempt to alter an exported input without creating a revision.
expected_persistent_result: Exports carry one stable period/revision identity, source-row identities, schema and hash; repeat does not create extra payables.
One payable NAD 1,875.00 and one separate employer obligation NAD 10.01 are imported under unique external references.
Unversioned mutation is rejected; a correction produces a documented new revision/adjustment handoff.
No export or import is labelled an internally validated country payroll calculation.
failure_result: Employer contribution reducing employee take-home, duplicate import or silent post-export edit fails the gate.

cases.title: Consume maintenance parts and fuel through Ledger exactly once
preconditions: Maintenance job J uses one part costing NAD 600.00, two labour hours at NAD 100.00 and contractor service NAD 400.00.
A separate fuel issue uses 20.000000 litres from sufficient stock.
cases.action: Finalize the authorized job costs and fuel issue, close J twice and inject a part-post failure in a separate run.
expected_persistent_result: J operational cost is NAD 1,200.00 with one reference to each approved cost source.
Part stock falls by one and fuel stock by 20.000000 litres exactly once; task closure creates no additional issues.
The failed required part-post run leaves job finalization and its synchronous effects uncommitted.
One next recurring maintenance occurrence is created for the completed occurrence key.
failure_result: Work owning a second fuel balance, duplicate recurrence or silent capitalization by the technician fails the gate.

cases.title: Record meter replacement and missing rainfall without false consumption
preconditions: Water meter M last valid reading is 1,000.000000 cubic metres; next is 1,020.000000.
Meter replacement then starts a new meter at 0.000000; next reading on the new meter is 5.000000.
One day has missing rainfall and another has measured 0.000000 mm.
cases.action: Post observations, explicit replacement and the daily water/rain report.
expected_persistent_result: Old-meter usage is 20.000000 cubic metres; new-meter usage is 5.000000; combined observed usage is 25.000000.
No negative 1,020.000000 use is created by replacement.
Missing rain remains missing; measured zero remains zero; no report asserts water entitlement from these observations.
failure_result: A decreasing reading without reset/replacement evidence is rejected or held for review, not silently converted to consumption.

cases.title: Activate only reviewed country capabilities and dated policy versions
preconditions: Namibia, South Africa and Botswana packs have separate capability/status/version records.
One capability is approved for its test profile; another remains draft with an unresolved local-law question.
cases.action: Activate the approved capability, attempt to activate the draft one, and switch transaction currency from NAD to ZAR on a draft.
expected_persistent_result: Only the approved tested capability activates with its country/version/effective date and reviewer evidence.
Draft capability remains disabled and creates no regulated posting/filing claim.
Changing transaction currency does not change legal-entity country, tax pack or functional currency.
failure_result: Treating currency selection as jurisdiction selection or importing sample rates as law fails the gate.

cases.title: Deduplicate provider callbacks and distinguish bank settlement
preconditions: A supported adapter contract defines signature verification, provider reference and event identity.
Payment intent P has no accepted settlement; callbacks include valid pending, valid settled, repeated settled and invalid-signature events.
cases.action: Deliver callbacks in that order, including a repeated valid settled event with a new transport request.
expected_persistent_result: Pending acknowledges intent only and creates no bank-settled claim.
One verified settled event records one payment/settlement effect under the provider identity.
Repeated event creates zero new payment effects; invalid signature changes no payment state.
External statement reconciliation remains separately attributable where required by the adapter.
failure_result: Accepting unsigned state changes, counting a pending acknowledgment as settled or duplicating a provider reference fails the gate.

cases.title: Recover outbox delivery after uncertain external acceptance
preconditions: A committed invoice owns one outbox intent with a stable event/delivery identity.
A controlled mail adapter accepts the message but loses the acknowledgment before local completion.
cases.action: Restart the worker and inspect/retry according to the adapter reconciliation policy.
expected_persistent_result: The invoice, stock, journal and payment records remain unchanged.
One durable intent retains attempts, uncertain outcome and available provider evidence; no new invoice is created.
The UI does not promise exactly-once email or recipient reading; any retry is recorded as another attempt under the same business intent.
failure_result: Sending before business commit, losing the intent or labelling uncertain acceptance as proven delivery fails the gate.

cases.title: Synchronize offline drafts without duplicate business posting
preconditions: Offline scope is limited to approved low-risk observations; device D captures a weight draft for animal A using persistent key K while disconnected.
No server weight_observation or other business effect exists for K; actor is currently authorised for A.
cases.action: Record a synthetic 421.500000 kg weight offline, reconnect and submit twice with D/K; lose the first successful response and retry the same key.
expected_persistent_result: The disconnected capture is visibly saved only on this device and creates no server record.
After current authorisation and version validation, exactly one weight_observation of 421.500000 kg exists for A; all replays return its original identity.
No stock movement, journal, invoice number or resource claim is created by the observation; local state becomes accepted only from the durable server result.
failure_result: Duplicate observations, a local draft labelled committed before server acceptance, or any offline financial/stock/reservation finalisation fails the gate.

cases.title: Revalidate stale offline data and revoked identity
preconditions: Device D has a permitted weight-observation draft against animal A version 7.
While disconnected A moves to a farm outside user U scope and becomes version 8; U access is revoked.
cases.action: Reconnect and attempt sync as U; later grant the appropriate current access and retry only after explicit stale-record review.
expected_persistent_result: Revoked U cannot read protected updates, retrieve a prior command result or create an observation.
After valid current authorisation the server detects version 7 vs 8 and presents review; no silent overwrite or scope escape occurs.
Only a reviewed new command for the current identity/version may create one observation; rejected drafts retain visible error status.
Local cache cleanup follows the approved retention/logout/revocation policy without claiming inaccessible lost-device data can be remotely erased.
failure_result: Cached permissions overriding server scope, silent version replacement or restricted documents/admin tokens in local drafts fails the gate.

cases.title: Upgrade supported module combinations without losing owned data
preconditions: Fixtures exist for Core+Ledger only and for all seven components; one domain is disabled but has historical records.
Each fixture has posted stock, trade, private-file links and stable application GUIDs.
cases.action: Upgrade from the last supported release using generated installers and controlled migrations, then re-enable the disabled domain and exercise a protected workflow.
expected_persistent_result: All pre-upgrade source identities, history, private-file links, quantities and monetary control totals remain unchanged.
Each migration records completion once; rerun applies no duplicate seed data, number allocation or business effect.
Disabled historical records stay readable under permission; re-enabled workflows resolve compatible services without duplicate classes.
failure_result: Partial DDL migration is reported as deployment failure with the documented recovery path; it is not claimed rolled back by a business transaction.

cases.title: Block destructive uninstall while dependencies or history exist
preconditions: Ledger contains posted documents; a satellite has retained historical source links; Core owns shared services and private files.
cases.action: Attempt to uninstall Core first and to remove a populated domain through ordinary extension management.
expected_persistent_result: Dependency-breaking uninstall is blocked or enters the explicitly documented non-destructive retention path.
No posted stock, journal, genealogy, booking or private evidence is cascade-deleted.
Existing history remains resolvable and the operator receives the precise dependency/data reason.
failure_result: Treating extension uninstall as permission to erase live business data fails the release gate.

cases.title: Restore a consistent business recovery point
preconditions: A supported backup captures database, private objects, configuration, JCB source/build references and one documented recovery cutoff.
Fixture includes posted transactions, one pending outbox intent and a private attachment checksum.
cases.action: Restore into an isolated new environment, reconcile controls and resume only the documented pending job.
expected_persistent_result: Recovered stock quantities/value, open invoice residuals, booking claims and posted journal control totals equal the captured cutoff.
Private attachment checksum and authorization match the captured evidence; no public exposure is introduced.
Resuming the pending job creates no duplicate financial effect and retains its delivery identity.
The run records actual recovery point and measured restoration duration against approved objectives.
failure_result: A downloaded ZIP without restored readback, inconsistent database/object cutoff or unverified business controls cannot pass.

cases.title: Demonstrate the declared pilot load without correctness loss
preconditions: Representative fixture has 1-5 farms, 10,000 individual animals, 100,000 operational events, 25,000 yearly stock lines and 20 accommodation resources.
An approved environment-specific latency/error budget is recorded before the run.
cases.action: Exercise 20 concurrent authorized active users with farm-scoped daily views and contested stock/booking writes, then reconcile committed results.
expected_persistent_result: Every successful request has one durable outcome; denied conflicts create zero partial effects.
Farm isolation holds and stock, room claims, invoice residuals and journal totals reconcile after the load.
The report records achieved latency percentiles and error counts against the pre-approved numerical budget; no capacity claim is inferred without those measurements.
failure_result: Unreconciled data, unbounded contention or an absent approved performance budget prevents this gate passing.

cases.title: Stage, validate and resume a migration import by stable row identity
preconditions: Import contains 100 source rows: 98 valid, one duplicate external identity and one unresolved required product reference.
No imported live records exist; mapping/schema version and source file hash are fixed.
cases.action: Run dry-run, resolve/reject the two problematic rows explicitly, import approved rows in bounded batches, interrupt after one batch and resume.
expected_persistent_result: Dry-run creates zero live business rows and exactly two actionable exception records.
After approved resolution, each accepted source row exists once with source identity and mapping version; rejected rows remain auditable.
Resume does not duplicate completed rows or effects; control totals match the accepted source population exactly.
failure_result: Silent row skipping, guessing required masters or rerun duplication fails cutover readiness.

cases.title: Activate native accounting with reconciled opening balances once
preconditions: Operational mode cutoff is approved; old export period is frozen.
Opening fixture: bank NAD 1,000.00, inventory NAD 500.00, AR NAD 200.00, AP NAD 300.00, customer deposits NAD 100.00 and opening equity NAD 1,300.00.
AR/AP detail, stock quantities/value and bank/deposit evidence match these amounts.
cases.action: Import opening detail and journals under unique cutover keys, activate native mode, repeat import and attempt a simple settings-toggle return to operational mode.
expected_persistent_result: Opening debits bank 1,000.00 + inventory 500.00 + AR 200.00 equal credits AP 300.00 + deposits 100.00 + equity 1,300.00, total NAD 1,700.00 each.
One opening source set persists; repeated import adds zero balances or effects.
Activation records approver/evidence/cutoff; native postings thereafter prevent a casual mode toggle back.
Historical invoices are not both replayed and represented again in imported opening residuals.
failure_result: Any control mismatch prevents activation; a balanced aggregate alone does not override unmatched AR/AP or stock detail.

cases.title: Release only the capabilities whose evidence is complete
preconditions: All intended release capabilities identify their country/profile, component versions and required acceptance case IDs.
Test evidence has been produced by the implementing team; this backlog itself still carries no execution claim.
cases.action: Review the release matrix, immutable build/source manifest, migration/restore receipts and owner/accountant/regional approvals before deployment.
expected_persistent_result: One release record lists exact included capabilities and their passing evidence revisions.
Any not_run, failed or unresolved blocking case keeps its dependent capability unshippable or disabled with a documented scope decision.
The published operator/runbook material includes backup restore, incident handling, updates, support ownership and data export.
No regulatory or performance claim exceeds the recorded country/environment evidence.
failure_result: A blanket all-ERP-complete label while accounting, regional or recovery gates remain open fails release acceptance.

cases.title: Canonicalize stock identity when optional dimensions are absent
preconditions: The declared balance key includes product, lot, warehouse/bin and ownership dimensions; lot/bin may be absent for an untracked item.
Two requests refer to the same logical absent lot/bin using the supported null/empty representations.
cases.action: Normalize both requests and create/lock the stock balance concurrently under the canonical non-null balance_key contract.
expected_persistent_result: Exactly one balance row exists for the logical untracked product/location/ownership identity.
Its canonical balance_key is non-null and identical for equivalent absent-dimension inputs; genuinely different ownership or location yields a different key.
The database uniqueness guard prevents duplicate rows without relying on NULL values comparing equal in a composite unique index.
failure_result: Duplicate null-dimension rows, normalization collisions across distinct owners or relying on unsupported partial-index behavior fails the gate.

cases.title: Rebuild projections without losing a concurrent committed movement
preconditions: Movement history sums to 10.000000 units/NAD 100.00 before the rebuild cutoff.
A concurrent authorized receipt adds 2.000000 units/NAD 20.00.
The chosen rebuild implementation explicitly uses either a writer quiesce or a versioned snapshot plus complete delta catch-up.
cases.action: Rebuild stock balance and valuation projections while scheduling the receipt at the boundary of snapshot and replacement.
expected_persistent_result: After rebuild/catch-up the authoritative history and published balance both equal 12.000000 units/NAD 120.00.
No committed receipt is overwritten by an older reconstructed snapshot; no receipt is counted twice.
The rebuild records its cutoff/version, completion watermark and strategy; no stale projection is advertised as current.
failure_result: Blindly replacing balances from a stale read or allowing a mixed old/new projection without freshness state fails the gate.

cases.title: Serialize pooled slot capacity through the existing physical resource
preconditions: One existing physical resource has approved capacity 3 for the requested slot and no active claims.
Two commands each request quantity 2 for the same slot through different package lines.
cases.action: Run both requests concurrently, locking that same existing resource row before reading or inserting overlapping claims.
expected_persistent_result: Exactly one request for quantity 2 commits; total active claimed quantity is 2 and remaining capacity is 1.
Both callers use the same physical resource lock; no unmodelled per-package or per-slot capacity owner is created.
The tested row-lock strategy does not assume exclusion constraints, partial indexes or the existence of a separate slot table.
failure_result: Both requests observing zero claims and reserving four units, or separate package-specific capacity totals, fails the gate.

cases.title: Block initial native-accounting activation until every control matches
preconditions: Operational mode has an approved proposed cutover and draft opening journal that balances globally.
AR detail is NAD 200.00 but the proposed AR control is NAD 190.00; another opening account contains an offsetting NAD 10.00 so aggregate debits and credits still balance.
cases.action: Attempt native activation, correct the mismatched source detail/control through an approved revision, and retry.
expected_persistent_result: The first activation is refused and operational mode remains active despite the globally balanced draft.
No final opening posting or native report availability is created until AR/AP, stock, bank/deposits/assets and approved mappings all reconcile.
After approved correction one activation record and one opening source set persist with cutoff, reviewer and evidence; the old export period is frozen.
This initial R2 control gate is repeated in the full migration rehearsal at M14.
failure_result: Treating aggregate balance as sufficient, automatic balancing plugs or native activation before accountant approval fails R2.

cases.title: Intersect independent stock holds without double-subtracting quantity
